source.citation: J. U. Andersen, E. Bonderup, E. Laegsgaard, B. B. Marsh and A. H. Sorensen, Nucl. Instrum. Methods 194, 209-224 (1982)
source.method: Table 2 transcribed; Figs. 8 and 11 digitized from a 400 dpi render of PDF pages 12-13 (axis ticks located by pixel search, markers by density/cross detection plus visual reading)

detector.geometry: photons detected in the beam direction
detector.solid_angle_note: 0.64e-6 x 4 pi sr (Fig. 11 caption; Fig. 12 caption prints 0.64e-5 x 4 pi, taken as a misprint since Sec. 7 gives ~1e-6 x 4 pi)

beam.divergence_note: Collimated to 0.02 deg FWHM; magnetic deflection 'may have contributed a similar amount during long runs'.
beam.energy_note: Measured energy about 1% below nominal; kinetic energies below are nominal.

notes: Rest-frame energy is E_R = E_lab / (2 gamma) for forward emission (Eq. 6). Fig. 8 abscissa gamma/d uses d(100) = 5.431, d(110) = 3.840, d(111) = 4.703 angstrom: these reproduce the nominal energies minus ~1% at every marker.
Fig. 8 markers digitized to about +-4 eV in E_R and +-0.01 in gamma/d. <100> markers at gamma/d 1.07 and 1.25 below the 2p-1s curve and 1.61 above it are 2p-1s/3p-1s as placed by the authors' curves.
Table 2 widths are Lorentzian half widths in the paper's notation Gamma (Eq. 27: Gamma = 2 gamma^2 hbar c (K_i + K_f)), i.e. FWHM of the lifetime Lorentzian; uncertainty 'at least 10%'.

Fig. 11 counts are fitted 2p-1s line areas for 1 uC per point into 0.64e-6 x 4 pi sr. Conversion: 1 count = 1 / (6.2415e12 e x 8.0425e-6 sr) = 1.992e-8 photons/sr/e. Crystal absorption was applied inside the line fit, so areas are absorption-corrected; detector efficiency is not stated. Digitization +-150 counts, +-0.003 deg. The data are slightly asymmetric about zero (peaks at -0.095 and +0.082 deg).
At exact alignment the 2p population vanishes (only s states are populated, Sec. 3); the measured ~4400 counts at 0.005 deg reflect beam divergence and scattering.

line_yield_fig11.theory_note: Many-beam and single-string curves include exponential 2p depopulation with decay length 0.44 um; both vanish at 0 deg.
